Savings is an important driver of member growth and retention, giving this role significant influence over the future of our financial health platform and how we help members build stronger financial futures. You’ll lead the ideation, development, launch, and scaling of new products and features while partnering closely with Engineering, Design, Data, Marketing, Legal, and Customer Support. This role reports to the Vice President & General Manager for Savings and Mobile. You’ll look for ways to use AI tools thoughtfully to accelerate product discovery, improve decision-making, reduce manual work, and create stronger member experiences. Who You Are The right fit looks like this You’re a curious and creative product leader who enjoys solving ambiguous problems and turning customer needs into clear product strategies. You communicate clearly, build alignment, and keep teams moving toward meaningful outcomes. jobs.title: Senior Product Manager, Test Preparation & Practice
jobs.description: At ACT, Your Work Makes a Difference Education has power -- a power that changes lives forever. It creates opportunities that lift up individuals, their families, and sparks societal change that echoes through generations to come. From our grassroots we have fought the good fight for inclusivity in education, and we remain devoted to helping anyone who struggles to access that power. This is what matters to us and we must do better -- we've never been more sure of our purpose. ACT team members are part of an organization dedicated to a mission that has never been more important: Helping people achieve education and workplace success. Advancing that mission within our organization, by helping our team members achieve education and workplace success of their own, is core to our values. ACT values a diverse workplace and is committed to fostering an inclusive environment in which every team member has an equal opportunity to grow. We want our team members to have the well-being and confidence they need to do their best work, in an environment where both they and ACT thrive. To support this, our total rewards include company paid life insurance, medical, dental, vision, flexible health and dependent spending accounts, 401(k) retirement savings with company match, paid holidays, paid time off, and so much more. We are seeking a Senior Product Manager, Test Preparation and Practice to help us fulfill that mission. This role owns the vision, strategy, and roadmap for test preparation and practice across ACT's full assessment portfolio -- including the ACT, PreACT, WorkKeys, and future assessments. This leader is accountable for growing revenue and access across ACT's free and paid test prep offerings, managing ACT's external test prep partners, and building products learners are willing to pay for. This role sits at the intersection of product, commercial strategy, and partnership management. The Senior Product Manager will define how free and paid test prep work together to bring more learners into the ACT ecosystem, grow wallet share against competing test prep providers, and increase customer lifetime value through a compelling prep and practice experience. The finalist will be hired at the salary and level commensurate with their qualifications. For this position, we anticipate offering an annual salary between $120,000 - $135,000. ACT manages salaries within this range based on relevant factors, including skills, experience, and internal equity. Location: This is a remote position, based in the United States. Visa: Applicants must be authorized to work in the U.S. without the need for visa sponsorship. What You Will Be Working On • Own the product vision, strategy, and roadmap for test preparation and practice across ACT's assessment portfolio, including the ACT, PreACT, WorkKeys, and future assessments. • Define the positioning and business model across ACT's free and paid test prep products -- balancing expanded access to free practice with sustained growth in paid product revenue. • Manage relationships with ACT's external test prep partners, driving joint roadmaps that grow revenue, improve existing products, and bring new offerings to market. • Evaluate and pursue new free or low-cost test prep partnerships to counter competitive threats and expand ACT's top-of-funnel reach, while protecting the value of ACT's paid portfolio. • Identify opportunities to capture greater wallet share from learners who currently spend on test prep with other providers. • Determine the right channel strategy for new practice tests and content -- owned portal, open web, paywalled digital product, or partner-exclusive distribution. • Lead the strategy for modernizing and repositioning ACT's existing signature test prep products, ensuring they remain differentiated and commercially competitive. • Define test prep and practice requirements specific to PreACT and WorkKeys, in addition to the ACT. • Partner with Marketing, Sales, and Market Research

jobs.title: Senior Technical Product Manager, Platform
jobs.description: Small businesses represent 99.9% of all companies, yet they're still forced to choose between clunky, outdated enterprise phone systems or their personal phones. This multi-billion dollar market has been overlooked for decades, left to cobble together solutions that slow them down instead of helping them grow. Quo is changing that. We bring calls, texts, and customer information together into one easy-to-use, AI-powered platform. We’re not just building a phone system. We’re setting a new standard for how businesses connect with their customers. Driven by our values, we move fast, build with determination, and obsess over delivering value to the businesses that have been underserved for far too long. Today, Quo is trusted by more than 120,000 companies and rated #1 in customer satisfaction on G2. We’re backed by Y Combinator, Tiger Global, Craft Ventures, Slow Ventures, and other top-tier investors. It’s safe to say we’re onto something big. About The Role Quo runs a real-time communications platform, and everything our customers experience — calls that connect instantly, messages that deliver reliably, integrations that just work — rests on infrastructure that has to be fast, resilient, and boring in the best possible way. This role owns the product direction for the two teams that make that possible: Scale & Reliability and Platform Engineering . You’ll treat platform and infrastructure as a product, with developer efficiency,reducing infrastructure-driven incidents and development risk as your North Star. You’ll set roadmap and priorities across reliability investment and platform capabilities, partner deeply with senior engineering leaders, negotiate with peer PMs, and make the hard tradeoffs between velocity, cost, and resilience explicit and defensible. You’ll be the connective tissue across engineering, product, and design, a force multiplier who turns strategy into a sequenced, funded, and delivered roadmap, keeping complex, multi-team programs on track from scoping through launch and retrospective. This is a technical PM role. You won’t write the code, but you’ll be fluent in the architecture, comfortable in a design review, and credible with staff and principal engineers. Some Of The Things You’ll Do • Own the business case for Platform — represent the team's priorities to executives and hold the roadmap accountable to measurable outcomes, not just delivery. • Own reliability as a product discipline — Service Level Objectives and platform health observability to reduce errors and incidents across our services, and negotiate with peer PMs to balance velocity with stability. • Build for the future — capacity planning ahead of growth, and the product side of incident management, from postmortem to funded fix. • Set the internal developer platform roadmap — paved paths, shared services, and self-serve tooling — with developer velocity and adoption as first-class metrics. • Hold the line on real-time performance — latency and media quality where milliseconds are the product. • Steer on the metrics that matter — uptime, latency, incident load, adoption, unit cost — using data and judgment to decide when to slow down and when to ship, and to make that case to product, engineering, and finance alike. • Run intake and prioritization of the Platform backlog — balancing business needs, technical requirements, and team capacity, and partnering with engineering leads to plan and staff initiatives. • Surface risks early and drive resolution — proactively identify technical risks, capacity constraints, and architectural gaps, and elevate to leadership with clear context and a recommended path forward.
